title: early-career-acceleration-and-mentor-rotation-guidelines-2027
author: Linnea Wu
summary: Guidelines to accelerate early-career hires through a structured microcurriculum, time-boxed mentor rotations, manager checkpoints, and measurable ramp metrics for consistent 90-day outcomes.
body:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a repeatable, low-friction program to accelerate early-career and junior hires (IC1–IC2 / L1–L2) to independent contribution within 90 days while distributing mentorship load across the organization. This document describes the microcurriculum, a 30/60/90 competency roadmap, mentor rotation mechanics, manager responsibilities, evaluation rubrics, and KPIs.

Scope
- Applies to all engineering, product, and data early-career new hires at Redwood Inference.
- Excludes senior hires with pre-existing role-specific ramp plans (handled by hiring manager).

Principles
- Time-boxed learning: short focused modules (1–3 days) to reduce context switching.
- Distributed mentorship: each hire rotates through 3 mentors to broaden network and avoid single-point-of-bias.
- Manager-owned outcomes: managers remain accountable for ramp milestones and performance check-ins.
- Measurable checkpoints: objective evidence (PRs, feature tickets, evals) required for milestone sign-off.

Quick reference: 30/60/90 outcomes
- Day 30 (Onboarded): dev environment + CI access, first small PR merged, 1 stakeholder intro, 3 microcurriculum modules complete.
- Day 60 (Contributing): regularly shipping small features or fixes, pair-programming on squad work, mentor feedback captured, 2 competency rubrics at "developing" or above.
- Day 90 (Independent): owns a modest feature or experiment end-to-end, demonstrates on-call readiness for low-severity issues, manager recommends transition to standard performance cycle.

Microcurriculum (recommended modules)
Use these 1–3 day modules to create a 4–6 module plan tailored to role. Managers pick at least 4 modules from the list below for the first 30 days.

| Module | Owner | Duration | Completion evidence | Notes |
|--------|-------|----------|---------------------|-------|
| Environment and CI basics | Engineering onboarding lead | 0.5 day | Local build + passing unit test | Scripted checklist and validation job |
| Codebase tour and core services | Squad tech lead | 1 day | Walkthrough recording + mapping doc | Include architecture diagram references |
| Small-feature ticket flow | Product ops | 0.5–1 day | One PR merged through full pipeline | Use starter ticket template |
| Observability & debugging | SRE mentor | 1 day | Reproduce and fix a minor alert in staging | Includes tracing quickstart |
| Security & data policies | Security team rep | 0.5 day | Acknowledgement of policy training | Required for private deployment access |
| API design & SDK usage | API guild lead | 1 day | Review and implement an example client call | Good for API-heavy roles |
| Model-serving primer | Serving runtime engineer | 1–2 days | Deploy a toy model to dev cluster | Guided exercise with checklist |

Mentor rotation mechanics
- Objective: expose the hire to 3 different perspectives within the first 60 days (technical, product/UX, and ops/infra or SRE).
- Rotation cadence: 2 weeks per mentor; overlap week with manager for context handoff.
- Mentor time commitment: ~4 hours/week for active rotation (pair sessions, code reviews, ad-hoc support).
- Mentor responsibilities:
  1) Schedule two structured pairing sessions per week (45–60 minutes).
  2) Leave written feedback in the hire's onboarding doc after each week.
  3) Complete the mentor short-form evaluation at rotation end (one-page rubric).

Manager checklist and cadence
- Pre-Start (hiring manager): confirm cohort modules, identify 3 mentors, create starter ticket and 30/60/90 measurable goals.
- Week 1: daily 1:1 for first 5 working days, ensure environment setup and first PR.
- Weeks 2–4: weekly 1:1 + weekly mentor sync; review microcurriculum evidence.
- Day 30: formal check-in — manager marks "Onboarded" or documents gaps with remediation plan.
- Day 60: competency review and adjust mentor assignments if needed.
- Day 90: manager completes final ramp evaluation and transitions employee to normal performance cycles.

Evaluation rubrics (short forms)
- Competency levels: Observed | Developing | Proficient | Strong
- Example criteria (Engineering): code correctness, test coverage, PR hygiene, domain knowledge, debugging speed.
- Minimum expected by Day 90: at least two criteria at "Developing" or higher; at least one tangible ownership item (ticket or feature) completed end-to-end.

Templates (copy to new hire onboarding page)
1) 30/60/90 Goals (manager to fill)
- 30 day goal: "Complete environment, merge first PR to staging, finish modules A/B/C."
- 60 day goal: "Ship two small features or experiments; lead one demo."
- 90 day goal: "Own feature X or experiment Y end-to-end; pass on-call readiness checklist."

2) Mentor feedback (weekly) - short form\- What did the hire do well this week?\- One specific improvement to focus on next week\- Suggested next pairing topic

Operational metrics and targets
- Target ramp-to-independence: median 90 days for early-career cohort.
- Day-30 success rate target: >= 85% (measured as environment+first PR merged).
- Mentor coverage goal: at least 95% of hires have three mentors assigned within 5 business days of start.
- Satisfaction target (new-hire survey @30d): average score >= 4.0/5.0.

Failure modes and remediation patterns
- Slow environment setup: escalation path — IT onboarding -> manager -> people-ops. If not resolved in 48 hours, assign temporary cloud dev environment.
- Low mentor engagement: replace mentor after 2 missed sessions; people-ops to mediate and reassign.
- Repeated competency gaps at Day 30: create a 30–60 remediation sprint with clear acceptance criteria and weekly check-ins.

Scaling and fairness considerations
- Rotations should balance mentor load: cap active mentees per mentor at 3 concurrent early-career hires.
- Standardize microcurriculum modules across squads to reduce variance in ramp quality.
- Document adjustments for remote hires (time-zone-friendly pairing windows, asynchronous feedback).

Operational playbook (step-by-step)
1) Hiring manager creates initial plan in Offer->Onboard checklist with selected modules and mentors (Day < 5 pre-start).
2) People-ops validates mentors and schedules cohort orientation (Day 0–1).
3) Mentor rotation schedule published to hire's onboarding page (Day 3).
4) Weekly evidence capture: mentors and hire populate the onboarding doc with short artifacts (PR links, screenshots, recordings).
5) Manager signs off Day 30/60/90 checkpoints or issues remediation plan (use template).

Related resources
- link: /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-immersion-rotation-playbook-2026 (mentor selection criteria)
- link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates (starter tickets & templates)
- link: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-readiness (on-call checklist)

Ownership
- People-ops: program design, templates, tracking and cohort analytics.
- Hiring manager: day-to-day execution, assigning mentors, signing off checkpoints.
- Mentors: weekly support and feedback.

Appendix A — Sample manager sign-off checklist
- Onboarding: environment, CI, repo access, team intros (Y/N)
- First PR merged: link
- Microcurriculum modules completed: list
- Mentor rotation completed: names and dates
- Competency notes: short bullet list
- Final recommendation: Onboarded / Remediation required / Extend mentoring

Appendix B — Survey questions (30-day)
1) I felt supported by my manager (1–5)
2) I felt supported by assigned mentors (1–5)
3) The microcurriculum prepared me for my role (1–5)
4) Time-to-first-PR was reasonable (1–5)
5) Open comments (free text)

Document maintenance
- People-ops to review and update this doc quarterly or after each cohort with >10% failure rate.
- Major changes require review by the Engineering onboarding lead and at least one manager reviewer.
